name: Arms Warrior
summary: Arms swings a slow, heavy two-hander for big hits and good cleave on two or three targets. It's slower-paced because Rage comes from weapon swings, and some of its kit (Spearing Strike, Mortal Strike) leans towards PvP.
statPriority: Hit, since misses deal no damage and give no Rage
Critical Strike (more damage and Rage; Agility adds some)
rotation: Dump spare Rage into Heroic Strike or Cleave
Hamstring only with Rage to spare
talents: Key picks: Bloodthrill, Improved Rend, Improved Overpower, Improved Slam, Mortal Strike, Impale, Two-Handed Specialization and Weaponmaster.
bestRaces: Orc: Attack Power cooldown + passive crit
Troll: attack speed cooldown, bonus vs beasts
Tauren: AoE stun, crit damage, Plainsrunning
forevChanges: Talent builds include 5 extra Legacy talent points. Rend now enables Bloodthrill procs.
tips: Never let Rage cap or hit zero
Keep Rend up at all times for Bloodthrill
Charge in from out of combat for free Rage
Pair Recklessness with big pulls
Blacksmithing + Engineering are the recommended professions

name: Fury Warrior
summary: Fury dual-wields, builds Rage from crits and spends it on Bloodthirst, Whirlwind and Heroic Strike, with strong cooldowns. It shines in PvE cleave fights but gives up survivability, so it's fragile and weak in PvP.
rotation: Dump spare Rage into Heroic Strike or Cleave
Optional: brief stance-dance for Rend and Overpower
talents: Key picks: Cruelty, Unbridled Wrath, Furious Precision, Dual Wield Specialization, Flurry, Enrage, Death Wish and Bloodthirst.
forevChanges: Rend scales better and Overpower costs little, so brief stance-dancing into Battle Stance can be worth it. Death Wish is Fury-only.
tips: Use a slow, heavy main-hand weapon
Don't Heroic Strike if it delays Bloodthirst or Whirlwind
Pair Recklessness with Death Wish for burst
Tell your tank when you'll Whirlwind packs
Berserker Rage breaks Fear and Incapacitate

name: Protection Warrior
summary: The classic plate-and-shield tank, relying on armour, cooldowns and crowd tools rather than mana or forms. Rage comes mostly from being hit, so it can run dry when nothing is hitting you.
statPriority: Hit, so swings land and make Rage
Stamina, armour and avoidance, balanced with threat stats
rotation: Dump spare Rage into Heroic Strike or Cleave
Keep Thunder Clap and Demoralizing Shout up
talents: Key picks: Shield Specialization, Anticipation and Deflection (feeding Master of Defense), Bastion, Cruelty, Improved Revenge, Defiance, Last Stand, Improved Shield Wall, Shield Slam and Vanguard (Charge in Defensive Stance).
bestRaces: Dwarf: Stoneform defensive cooldown + crit damage
Night Elf: crit cooldown, dodge, speed
Orc: Attack Power cooldown, magic defensive
forevChanges: Shields are genuinely worth using in Forever for threat and survival, unlike other Classic versions. Vanguard lets you Charge in Defensive Stance.
tips: Charge to open pulls for instant Rage
Challenging Shout keeps aggro through taunt immunity
Keep Sunder, Thunder Clap, Demo Shout and Rend running
Use Bloodrage freely
Wear Mail until 40, then Plate

name: Balance Druid
summary: No longer a joke spec: Balance is a solid caster DPS using DoTs and hard casts, plus buffs, debuffs and emergency healing. Eclipse gives it a satisfying Starfire/Wrath rhythm.
statPriority: Hit (Nature's Reach covers a lot early)
rotation: 2-4 targets: DoT everything, filler on priority target
Refresh DoTs or Faerie Fire while moving
talents: Standard 41/0/10: Improved Wrath, Moonglow and Eclipse, plus Genesis, Insect Swarm, Improved Starfire and Moonkin Form.
forevChanges: Eclipse adds a Wrath/Starfire rhythm, Hurricane has no cooldown, and DoTs update dynamically with buffs (no snapshotting).
tips: Don't clip DoTs
Skip DoTs on mobs about to die
Spend Clearcasting on Starfire
Don't downrank
Save Innervate for a healer in endgame

name: Feral Druid
summary: Feral can deal melee damage in Cat Form or tank in Bear Form, and both are viable. Far fewer awkward mechanics than in Classic, but juggling forms and resources still takes skill.
rotation: Ferocious Bite at 4-5 combo points with 70+ Energy
Refresh Rake right after it drops
Shifting Power on cooldown under 50 Energy
Build combo points with Shred (Claw if you can't get behind)
talents: Hybrid 9/37/5 for both cat DPS and bear tanking: Feral Charge, Lacerate, Predatory Discipline, Leader of the Pack, Shifting Power and Primal Bite.
bestRaces: Tauren: AoE stun usable in form, extra health
forevChanges: Powershifting and bear-weaving are gone, so stay in one form. You can now use consumables and talk to most NPCs without leaving form.
tips: Refresh bleeds just after they expire
Stay behind targets for Shred
Cower to drop threat
Turn on the Personal Resource Display to see mana in form
Feral Charge closes gaps and interrupts

name: Restoration Druid
summary: Heals mostly with heal-over-time spells on one or several targets. It needs more planning than other healers because HoTs go out in advance, but brings great utility.
rotation: Swiftmend a target that already has Rejuvenation or Regrowth
Wild Growth when several people take damage
Rejuvenation on anyone under sustained damage
Healing Touch at a rank that covers the gap
Nature's Swiftness for an instant big heal
talents: Standard 13/0/38: Reflection for mana, Bloom for extra healing when HoTs expire, Wild Growth.
forevChanges: New Wild Growth AoE HoT, Swiftmend no longer eats your HoT, Reflection is buffed, a new out-of-combat rez (Revive), and Faerie Fire for Restoration.
tips: Don't clip HoTs
Downrank Healing Touch to save mana
Turn on mouseover casting
Only start Tranquility if you can channel it fully
Bring a Camping crit buff if you're the only Druid

name: Beast Mastery Hunter
summary: Your pet does a big share of the damage and can tank pulls, which makes Beast Mastery excellent for solo play. Its weakness is relying on the pet staying alive and on target.
statPriority: Hit (9% at 300 weapon skill, 6% at 305, vs level 63 bosses)
Critical Strike (pets inherit all of it)
rotation: Pre-place Immolation Trap where the tank will stand
Pre-cast Aimed Shot, then use it on cooldown
Summon Hawk on cooldown, keep two out
Arcane Shot once two Hawks are up
Rapid Fire and Bestial Wrath on cooldown
AoE: Multi-Shot, Explosive Trap, spread Serpent Sting
talents: 31/20/0: Bestial Discipline, Bestial Wrath, Careful Aim (Intellect to AP), Focused Fire, Unleashed Fury, Ferocity and Frenzy.
bestRaces: Troll: attack speed, bonus vs beasts
forevChanges: New spells and talents, consolidated Classic talents, reworked Bestial Discipline; Scorpid Sting now lowers the target's hit chance by 2% for 20 sec.
tips: Use Stay and Move To to keep your pet safe
Mind the dead zone between melee and 8 yards
Don't move unnecessarily (it breaks Auto Shot)
Stay in Aspect of the Hawk
Tranquilizing Shot removes Enrage/Frenzy
Feign Death to reset bad pulls

name: Marksmanship Hunter
summary: Strong long-range damage, with or without a pet: the new Lone Wolf talent trades your pet for more personal damage in endgame PvE. The rotation is simple; positioning, mana and cooldown timing matter.
rotation: Pre-cast Sniper Shot, then use it on cooldown
AoE: Multi-Shot, Serpent Sting on all, Explosive Trap
talents: 5/46/0: Lethal Attacks, Barrage, Careful Aim, Rapid Recuperation for mana, Sniper Shot; Lone Wolf (swap for Improved Tracking to keep a pet).
forevChanges: New Lone Wolf talent (give up your pet for damage) and new top-tier Sniper Shot ability.
tips: Stay in Aspect of the Hawk
Keep Auto Shot going: avoid needless movement
Sniper Shot and Aimed Shot are mana-hungry
Keep Feign Death ready when petless
Stable a few pets for tough solo content

name: Survival Hunter
summary: Survival weaves melee into its ranged rotation or fights fully in melee, with new talents boosting melee strikes and traps. Demanding positioning and timing, but high damage potential.
rotation: Back to range and repeat shots
talents: 5/13/33: Savage Strikes, Clever Traps, Resourcefulness, Careful Aim; Lone Wolf (or Efficiency / Improved Stings to keep a pet).
forevChanges: New melee and trap talents, consolidated Classic talents, reworked Scorpid Sting (lowers enemy hit chance).
tips: Reach the hit cap
Take Resourcefulness for mana while weaving
Stay in Hawk or Beast aspect, not travel aspects
Keep your quiver/ammo pouch upgraded
